summary: A humorous column by Jamie Tunstall on how technology is reshaping neighborhood life, covering delivery drones, robotic pets, AI smart homes, social media feuds, eco gadgets, and a planned automated festival. It mixes anecdotes about neighbors' tech mishaps with a lighthearted view that the changes, hiccups included, are ultimately a good thing.
one_line: Jamie Tunstall's humorous column on how drones, robot pets, smart homes, and social media are changing neighborhood life.
key_facts: The column was written by Jamie Tunstall and published September 5, 2023.
The Joneses' new SmartDrone fetches their online shopping, and rumor says they are programming it to pick up lattes.

Timmy Merton's rogue drone, controlled by a smartphone, swooped down the street and nearly hit Mrs. Thompson's prized rosebush, prompting the neighborhood to form a council for 'Air Traffic Rules for Dockets and Drones'.
On September 15, 2023, the Millers introduced their robotic dog "Rufus", and soon everyone wanted a robot pet.
The Macintyre residence has an AI house assistant named "Bobby" that manages lights and predicts when they will run out of toilet paper.
Herbert Bloomington, aged 86, accidentally set off his home security system while trying to turn up the volume on a gardening show, resulting in a SWAT team descending on his petunias.
Miss Eunice Weatherby, head of the local watch group, now spends her evenings decoding firewall updates, and the watch is considering the name 'Neighborhood Watch: Cyber Edition'.
Charlie Henderson's barbeque went viral after he accidentally grilled his smartphone along with the ribs, earning 10,000 likes.
Neighbors feud on platforms like Faceplace, Twibble, and InMySpace using hashtags such as #NoisyNeighbors and #LawnWars.
Allen Greaves converted his mailbox into a charging station for passersby's mobile devices, promoting "juice for the journey".
Nina Patel's holographic yoga instructor performs on her front lawn each morning.

On November 3, 2023, the Neighborhood Association unveiled plans for an 'Automated Annual Festival' with self-cooking hot dogs, drones choreographed to Beethoven's Symphony No. 9, and a "Robo-Raffle".
